page: Microsoft Azure D48a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 7763 processor under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features an x86_64 architecture offering 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores at 3.525 GHz. It includes a standard cache layout with 32 KB L1 data, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity stands at 192.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with 0 GPUs provisioned, but the instance bundles 1288 GB of local SSD temporary storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel computational performance alongside top-tier memory metrics. The instance achieves a PassMark memory score of 3004.59, landing in the top 10% tier. Multi-core execution ranks in the top 25% across tests, including stress-ng multi-core (64,905.97), Geekbench multi-core (16,290.0), PassMark CPU (52,694.99), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (218.56 GB/sec). Single-threaded tasks, such as Geekbench single-core (1,613.0) and gzip compression (25.91 GB/sec), place primarily within the middle 50% tier, showing that throughput relies heavily on multi-threaded utilization.

Data throughput and specialized workload capabilities reflect balanced performance. The EPYC architecture integrates cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI flags, leading to a strong PassMark encryption score of 51,712.75. However, the CPU lacks AVX-512 extensions and advanced matrix accelerators. While smaller AI workloads like 135M model text generation operate within the top 25% (276.09 tokens/sec), larger models face bottlenecks, with 70B model text generation dropping to 2.7 tokens/sec in the bottom 25%. Local SSD performance supports general I/O, recording 47.18 million operations/sec on Redis SET operations and 30.2 GB/sec in static web serving.

Cost efficiency is centered on dense CPU and memory allocation without dedicated GPU overhead. By providing 48 threads and 192 GB of RAM alongside integrated high-capacity local SSD storage, it serves well for scale-out applications, build servers, multi-threaded data processing, relational databases, and enterprise web-tier applications.
description: Microsoft Azure D48a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores, paired with 192.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per vCPU) and 1288 GB of local SSD storage, without GPU acceleration. The instance displays solid multi-threaded performance, ranking in the top 25% across stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks, alongside a top-10% PassMark memory score of 3004.59. It features hardware-accelerated cryptography with AES and SHA-NI support, although it lacks AVX-512 extensions, impacting large-model machine learning inference. With its balanced memory ratio and dedicated core density, the D48a_v4 fits multi-threaded data processing, enterprise relational databases, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and demanding web services.
